clue.text: It's a long journey from Turkey to eastern Cambodia

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle registration code for Turkey
K is Cambodia's vehicle registration code, from its former name Kampuchea

explanation.surface: A traveller describes the long haul overland from Turkey to the far east of Cambodia.
explanation.walkthrough: Both countries are given by their international car registration letters; Cambodia's K dates from when it was called Kampuchea.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an arduous expedition on foot or overland is a trek.

clue.text: Item of clothing obtained from outfitter

definitions.text: Item of clothing obtained from outfitter

indicators.note: the first three letters of the shop word outfitter double as the signal that the rest of that word is put out of order

explanation.surface: A shopper picks up a garment from a tailor's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a hat bought at a clothier's, while inside 'outfitter' the 'out' tells you to rearrange 'fitter'. TITFER is Cockney rhyming slang (tit for tat = hat).
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang for a hat, a piece of headwear one might buy from a clothier.

clue.text: One car is written off in storyline

indicators.note: a car that is written off is wrecked, so the letters of the preceding words are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A plot summary in which a single vehicle is declared a write-off after a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the outline of a plot or a sequence of imagined events is a storyline.

clue.text: Throwing a game

definitions.meaning: the Irish stick-and-ball field sport played with a hurley and sliotar

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of deliberately losing a match, of throwing a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throwing a game' reads as match-fixing, but it splits into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the present participle of flinging forcefully; the other is the Irish field sport, part of this puzzle's Irish theme.

clue.text: Setter finally flips, seeing US TV network

indicators.note: the final pair of letters of the setter's name are turned round

parts.note: the setter of this puzzle is Hob

explanation.surface: The puzzle-setter loses their temper when watching an American television channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last two letters are swapped: H stays put and the final OB is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Home Box Office is an American cable and satellite television channel, known by its initials.

clue.text: Wine provided by good parties

parts.note: raves are wild dance parties

explanation.surface: Good parties come supplied with plenty of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Graves is a Bordeaux region whose red and white wines bear its name.

clue.text: Amount of money once put on queen and joker changing hands

indicators.note: left is swapped for right, so one letter for the left hand gives way to the letter for the right

parts.note: a clown is a joker or comedian

explanation.surface: Cash used to be staked on the queen and the joker in a card game, as they passed between players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on queen' is a second, cryptic definition: a crown is placed on a queen's head. 'Changing hands' turns L (left) into R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: The crown was a pre-decimal British coin worth five shillings, so a sum of money no longer in use.

clue.text: One famous film star, initially with Native American name in real life

indicators.note: the opening letters of the four words before it are taken

parts.note: the Cree are an indigenous people of North America

explanation.surface: A celebrated movie actor, with a Native American name, as they are away from the cameras.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: what happens away from the cameras is a performer's private, real life rather than their screen life.

clue.text: In Africa, money not available to terrorists

parts.note: the IRA, the Irish Republican Army, a paramilitary group

explanation.surface: Funds in Africa are kept out of the hands of terrorist groups.
explanation.definitionFit: The naira is the currency of Nigeria, so it is African money.

clue.text: Bung in meat, cold, for picnic's starter

indicators.note: the cold letter is put in place of the picnic's opening letter

parts.note: pork is a meat

indicators.note: the first letter of the word picnic is the one taken

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A picnic's first course is cold meat with a bung in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a stopper for a bottle, made of bark, is a bung.

clue.text: Poem about girl going both ways, originally feminist activist in Liberal party

indicators.note: taken to mean turned round, so the poem's title is read backwards

parts.note: If is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem

indicators.note: the girl's name reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name

indicators.note: the opening letters of feminist, activist, in and Liberal are taken

explanation.surface: A poem concerning a girl who swings both ways, written by a pioneer feminist campaigner in the Liberal party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a placement indicator but is one of the four words whose first letters are taken; 'Liberal party' is not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Fianna Fáil is the Irish political party that Jack Lynch led, central to this puzzle's theme.

clue.text: Today it's Hob 50, written for special character

indicators.note: a symbol is put down in place of another, a substitution

parts.note: Hob is the compiler of today's puzzle, its setter
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Hob celebrates a milestone fiftieth puzzle today, composed for a special person.
explanation.walkthrough: This was Hob's 50th Independent puzzle, so the clue is a self-referential nod.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a single symbol of an alphabet is called a character.

clue.text: Ego not foremost for Hob, possibly

indicators.note: the word loses its leading letter

parts.note: one's ego is one's self

explanation.surface: The setter Hob admits to being, perhaps, not the most egotistical.
explanation.walkthrough: Hob is the setter's pseudonym, but here it is a hobgoblin; 'possibly' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A hob, short for hobgoblin, is a mischievous sprite, one kind of little folkloric creature.

clue.text: Is love cheat going out with a prime minister?

indicators.note: the letters are put out of their order, rearranged

parts.note: O, the zero score in tennis, is love

explanation.surface: A scandal question: is a love rat dating a head of government?
explanation.definitionFit: The Taoiseach is the head of the Irish government, Ireland's equivalent of a premier.

clue.text: In Brussels, official route a Roman Catholic negotiated

indicators.note: a route that is negotiated is worked through, here meaning the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A Catholic in Brussels navigating a path through the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureaucrat of the European Union, whose institutions are based in Brussels.

clue.text: Features of weather in Leeds, say

definitions.meaning: boundaries between air masses on a forecast chart
the city name Leeds sounds like 'leads', and leads in a race are positions at the head

explanation.surface: A forecaster describes the weather systems over the Yorkshire city of Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals that Leeds stands for its sound-alike 'leads'; in, in front, and leading all mean the same position. Leeds is a city in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteorological boundaries between warm and cold air shown on weather maps; also positions at the head, like leads.

clue.text: Fresh pâté on tray, prepared for afternoon get-together

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second
a fresh version of the word pâté is a new arrangement of its letters
the word tray is made up anew, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Fresh pâté is set on a tray, ready for an afternoon gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: 'Fresh' rearranges PATE into TEAP, and 'prepared' rearranges TRAY into ARTY; 'on' stacks one above the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A social gathering in the afternoon at which the drink served is tea, with cakes and sandwiches.

clue.text: In truth, one's too scrupulous

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that, truthfully, they are overly conscientious.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: someone scrupulous is truthful and upright in their dealings.

clue.text: Support from unnamed youth

indicators.note: the letter for name is removed

parts.note: a teen is a young person

explanation.surface: An anonymous young person offers help.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf peg holding the ball up for driving is a small support.

clue.text: Cavity in which poor Hob starts falling off a motorbike?

indicators.note: the indicated letters drop away from the motorbike

parts.note: Triumph is a British motorcycle make

indicators.note: the first letters of poor and Hob are taken

explanation.surface: A sorry tale of the setter Hob tumbling off a motorcycle.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the motorbike as an example of a make, Triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: An anatomical term for a chamber of the heart, so a body cavity.

clue.text: Someone that's very good, taking part in school play

parts.note: a class is a division of a school
to act is to play a role

explanation.surface: A star pupil who has a role in the school drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase also suggests an item performed by a class in a school show.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a person of outstanding quality or skill is described as a class act.

clue.text: Bet the barmaid wants Marilyn Chambers' part

indicators.note: only a portion of the run of words is taken

explanation.surface: A barmaid fancies a role played by a film actress.
explanation.walkthrough: Bet Lynch was the brassy barmaid of the Rovers Return in Coronation Street, a long-running British TV soap. Jack Lynch is the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Bet's surname in the soap: the full name of the fictional pub landlady character.

clue.text: Great St Bernard, say, with barrel (large) round neck in first half

indicators.note: the barrel and large letters go around the next piece

parts.note: a tun is a large cask

indicators.note: only the first half of the word neck is used

explanation.surface: A St Bernard dog with its barrel of brandy around its neck.
explanation.walkthrough: The St Bernard looks like the dog with a brandy keg; the Great St Bernard is an Alpine pass with a road tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Great St Bernard Tunnel runs under the Alps between Switzerland and Italy.

clue.text: Hard of hearing

definitions.meaning: describing the hearing of a case in court, where a judge is judging the accused

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard of hearing' reads as deaf, but it splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: something difficult is wearing, and a court hearing is the process of judging a case.

clue.text: Fashionable position showing weakness

parts.note: something fashionable is in
one's capacity is one's role or position

explanation.surface: Being in vogue reveals a vulnerability.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: inability or lack of power is a weakness.

clue.text: Sailor in old children's TV series, letting off firework

indicators.note: the firework is let off, released from the title

parts.note: Crackerjack was a long-running BBC children's show
a cracker is a firework that bangs

explanation.surface: A sailor in a vintage children's programme sets off a firework.
explanation.walkthrough: Crackerjack was a BBC children's variety show from 1955 to 1984. Jack, a slang term for a sailor, also recalls Jack Lynch.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack, short for Jack Tar, is a traditional slang term for a seaman.

clue.text: Jump from plane over Spain

indicators.note: in a down clue the plane is placed above

parts.note: a fast turbine-powered airliner, a common word for a plane
E is Spain's international vehicle code, from España

explanation.surface: A parachutist leaps out of an aircraft above Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet leap from one foot to the other is a jeté, a kind of jump.

clue.text: My grain's been cropped

indicators.note: the word has had its tail cut off, losing its final letter

parts.note: corn is grain

explanation.surface: A farmer's lament that the grain has been harvested.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise; 'my!' and 'cor!' are interjections, the latter British slang.

clue.text: Hot one-two that's used by drummers

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
I is the Roman numeral for one
refers to the answer at 2 down, rhyming slang for headgear

explanation.surface: A hot one-two combination is something drummers rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two' points to 2 down, Cockney slang for a hat. 'one-two' looks like a boxing combination.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum kit component: a pair of cymbals clashed together by a foot pedal, played by drummers.

clue.text: Cheese turns mouldy, even starts going off

indicators.note: milk going off turns sour, and here the letters go off into a new order
the opening letters of mouldy and even are taken

explanation.surface: A cheese turns mouldy, and even begins to go rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Munster is a soft, strong-smelling washed-rind cheese from Alsace.
